Before the movie starts

5

Five names,
five different jobs

A field guide to the company logos that flash by before a Bollywood film starts — and what each one actually does.

You've seen it before: four or five company names scroll past before a single frame of story. In Bollywood, the lineup looks a bit different from Hollywood — music labels get their own card, the "Presented By" credit does a lot of heavy lifting, and the same banner often wears multiple hats. Here's what each role actually means.

The lineup

5

Role · "Presented By" Credit

The prestige card — intentionally vague

This is usually the first and most prominent card. It can mean the distributor, a senior producer's banner lending its brand, a co-financier, or all three at once. It's a negotiated prestige credit and Bollywood uses it far more heavily than Hollywood does.

"Yash Raj Films presents"

Top 5 you'll recognize

4

Role · Production Company

Actually made the film

The banner that hired the crew, ran the set day-to-day, and answered for the budget. In Bollywood, these are often personality-driven family operations — a star's or director's own house — rather than the faceless corporate shingles you see in Hollywood.

"A Dharma Productions Film"

Top 5 you'll recognize

Rajkumar Hirani Films
3

Role · Distributor

Gets it into theaters (and often does much more)

Books the film into theaters, handles marketing, and picks the release date. In Bollywood, some banners run their own nationwide distribution networks rather than licensing to a separate company. When you see a different distributor for "Hindi theatrical" vs "overseas," that's territory-by-territory distribution at work.

"Distributed by PEN Marudhar"

Top 5 you'll recognize

AA Films
2

Role · Music Label

Owns the soundtrack — a revenue engine on its own

This is the big one that has no real equivalent in Hollywood. Music rights are a major revenue stream in Indian cinema — labels often pay crores for the rights before the film is even finished, and the songs generate income for years via streaming, radio, and ringtones. The music label always gets its own card.

"Music on T-Series"

Top 5 you'll recognize

Sony Music India

T-Series alone has over 250 million YouTube subscribers — music isn't a side business in Bollywood, it's often the business.

1

Not a company · Possessory Credit

"A Film By ___" is a person, not a company

Less common in Bollywood than in Hollywood, but you'll see it with directors who've built a strong auteur reputation. It's a negotiated contractual credit naming the director as the film's principal author.

"A Sanjay Leela Bhansali Film"

Directors you'll see it with

Sanjay Leela Bhansali Rajkumar Hirani S.S. Rajamouli Anurag Kashyap Zoya Akhtar

— and roll film —

Worth knowing

One company, many hats

  • T-SeriesMusic label, production house, and distributor — the full Bollywood triple threat.
  • Yash Raj FilmsProduction, distribution through its own nationwide network, and its own music label (YRF Music).
  • Dharma ProductionsProduction house that often co-finances its own slate and co-distributes with a studio partner.
  • Viacom18 StudiosFinances, produces, and distributes — backed by Reliance-controlled Viacom18.
  • Reliance EntertainmentCorporate financier that also produces and co-distributes, especially for bigger-budget films.

Bollywood vs Hollywood — key difference: In Hollywood, the "Presented By" credit and the distributor are usually separate companies. In Bollywood, a single banner often presents, produces, finances, and distributes — making that first card more like a stamp of ownership than a specific job description.

Also worth spotting: "In association with" in a Bollywood context usually signals a co-financier or co-producer who put up part of the budget but didn't run the production.
